findings.title: Prohibited Diffie-Hellman group 2 (1024-bit MODP)
findings.detail: 1024-bit MODP: within reach of nation-state precomputation (Logjam). A single precomputation against a standard modulus breaks every session that ever used it, including traffic already recorded.
findings.reference: RFC 8247 s2.4; NIST SP 800-77 Rev. 1 s3.3
findings.remediation: Configure Group 19 (256-bit ECP) or Group 14 at minimum.

findings.title: Association provides only 80-bit security
findings.detail: Component strengths: encryption 128 bits, prf 96 bits, integrity 96 bits, key_exchange 80 bits. The association is bounded by its key_exchange at 80 bits, which is graded 'deprecated'. A strong cipher does not compensate for a weak key exchange: an attacker who recovers the session key never has to attack the cipher at all.
findings.remediation: Raise the key_exchange to at least the 128-bit level. The whole suite should be re-specified together rather than patched component by component.

findings.title: ESP tunnel using AES-CBC with 96-bit ICV
findings.subject: 203.0.113.55->198.51.100.77:0x52e17fd9
findings.detail: Packet framing on this SA matches block 16, IV 16, ICV 12, which identifies AES-CBC-128 / HMAC-SHA1-96. SHA-1 truncated to 96 bits; CBC lacks integrated authentication. Inferred from 420 packets at 100% confidence in the framing class.
findings.reference: RFC 4303 s2; RFC 8221; NIST SP 800-77 Rev. 1 s4.1
findings.remediation: Reconfigure the child SA proposal to AES-GCM-256 and confirm from the gateway's own SA table.

findings.title: Deprecated integrity algorithm: AUTH_HMAC_SHA1_96
findings.detail: SHA-1 is deprecated for new systems (SP 800-131A Rev. 2)

findings.title: No quantum-resistant key establishment
findings.detail: The SA relies entirely on classical Diffie-Hellman. Traffic recorded today can be decrypted once a cryptanalytically relevant quantum computer exists, which matters for material whose sensitivity outlives the hardware.
findings.remediation: Deploy an RFC 8784 post-quantum pre-shared key now, and enable a hybrid ML-KEM key exchange (Group 35-37) as gateway firmware allows.

findings.title: Broken transforms remain in the proposal set
findings.detail: The initiator advertised transforms that policy prohibits: DH group 2. Even unselected, they widen the downgrade surface — an on-path attacker who can drop the strong proposals may force a fallback.
findings.remediation: Prune the gateway's transform set to approved algorithms only, so a downgrade has nothing to fall back to.

findings.title: Repeated negotiation failures observed
findings.detail: The exchange carried NO_PROPOSAL_CHOSEN. In isolation this is a misconfiguration; in volume it is the signature of an attacker probing which proposals a gateway will accept, or brute-forcing authentication.
findings.remediation: Correlate against the gateway's own logs and rate-limit IKE from untrusted sources. If unexplained, treat as reconnaissance.

findings.title: Deprecated PRF: PRF_HMAC_SHA1
findings.detail: SHA-1-based PRF is deprecated for new systems

findings.title: IKEv2 fragmentation not negotiated
findings.detail: Neither peer advertised RFC 7383 fragmentation. Certificate-bearing IKE_AUTH messages then rely on IP fragmentation, which middleboxes on carrier paths routinely drop — a common cause of tunnels that establish with PSK but fail with certificates.
findings.remediation: Enable IKEv2 fragmentation on both peers before migrating to certificate auth.

throughput.note: Measured single-threaded in the pure-Python reference reader. The C++/DPDK ingestion path is a separate component; this figure is the portable path's real rate, not a line-rate claim.

assumptions.note: The CRQC arrival estimate is a planning assumption, not a prediction. Substitute the agency's own figure; the ranking of links is unchanged by it, only the urgency framing.

links.rationale: MODP key exchange at 80 classical bits and zero quantum bits. Every session key on this link is recoverable by Shor's algorithm from recorded traffic.

phases.action: Replace broken classical cryptography first. These links are exposed to a conventional attacker today, so the quantum timeline is not the binding constraint — fix them regardless of PQC readiness.
phases.target: AES-GCM-256, DH Group 19 or 31, IKEv2, certificate auth

remediation.strongswan:
# CipherGuard hardening plan - strongSwan (swanctl)
# Generated 2026-09-19T05:16:43+00:00 from capture 'downgrade.pcap'
# Posture score 27/100 (grade E) - 1 critical, 1 high
#
# REVIEW BEFORE APPLYING. Staged as new policy entries; nothing existing
# is removed. Cut over during a change window, verify the tunnel
# re-establishes, then retire the old policy.
#
# Findings addressed by this plan:
#   [critical] IKE-006 (observed) Prohibited Diffie-Hellman group 2 (1024-bit MODP)
#   [high    ] IKE-012 (observed) Association provides only 80-bit security
#   [medium  ] ESP-001 (inferred) ESP tunnel using AES-CBC with 96-bit ICV
#   [medium  ] IKE-005 (observed) Deprecated integrity algorithm: AUTH_HMAC_SHA1_96
#   [medium  ] IKE-007 (observed) No quantum-resistant key establishment
#   [medium  ] IKE-008 (observed) Broken transforms remain in the proposal set
#   [medium  ] IKE-010 (observed) Repeated negotiation failures observed
#   [low     ] IKE-005 (observed) Deprecated PRF: PRF_HMAC_SHA1
#   [low     ] IKE-011 (observed) IKEv2 fragmentation not negotiated
#
connections {
    cg-hardened {
        version = 2
        proposals = aes256gcm16-prfsha256-ecp256
        dpd_delay = 30s
        rekey_time = 86400s
        # RFC 8784 post-quantum pre-shared key: deploy now so traffic
        # recorded today is not decryptable by a future quantum attacker.
        ppk_id = cg-ppk-primary
        ppk_required = no
        local {
            auth = pubkey
            certs = gateway-cert.pem
        }
        remote {
            auth = pubkey
        }
        children {
            cg-child {
                esp_proposals = aes256gcm16-ecp256
                rekey_time = 28800s
                mode = tunnel
            }
        }
    }
}

# Refuse weak algorithms outright rather than merely preferring strong ones,
# so a downgrade attempt has nothing to fall back to.
